# pangolin_resource_policy (Resource)

Manages a shared Pangolin resource policy: SSO, role and user grants, email whitelist and access rules that several HTTP resources can share. Attach a resource to it with `resource_policy_id` on `pangolin_resource`.

Secrets are managed by separate resources so they never travel with the policy: `pangolin_resource_policy_password`, `pangolin_resource_policy_pincode` and `pangolin_resource_policy_header_auth`.

> **Note:** Resource policies require Pangolin Enterprise (a valid license with the resource policies feature). The org admin role is always granted by the server and is not listed in `role_ids`. A policy cannot be destroyed while a resource is still attached to it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pangolin_domains" "all" {}

# Shared access settings for every internal tool (Pangolin Enterprise).
resource "pangolin_resource_policy" "internal" {
  name     = "internal-tools"
  sso      = true
  role_ids = [pangolin_role.devs.id]
  user_ids = [pangolin_user.alice.id]

  email_whitelist_enabled = true
  whitelist_emails        = ["*@example.com"]

  apply_rules = true
  rules = [
    { action = "ACCEPT", match = "CIDR", value = "10.0.0.0/8", priority = 1 },
    { action = "DROP", match = "COUNTRY_IS_NOT", value = "FR", priority = 2 },
    { action = "DROP", match = "METHOD", value = "DELETE", priority = 3, enabled = false },
  ]
}

# Attach resources to the policy. Remove `resource_policy_id` to
# detach a resource and fall back to its own inline policy.
resource "pangolin_resource" "wiki" {
  name               = "wiki"
  subdomain          = "wiki"
  domain_id          = data.pangolin_domains.all.domains[0].domain_id
  resource_policy_id = pangolin_resource_policy.internal.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the policy.

### Optional

- `apply_rules` (Boolean) Evaluate `rules` for requests to the attached resources. Defaults to `false`.
- `email_whitelist_enabled` (Boolean) Enable the email (one-time password) whitelist. Defaults to `false`.
- `nice_id` (String) Readable ID, unique per org. Generated by the server when unset.
- `role_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of the roles granted access. The org admin role is always granted and must not be listed.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Access rules, evaluated by priority. The whole list is replaced on every change. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `skip_to_idp_id` (Number) Bypass the Pangolin login page and jump straight to the given IdP of the org.
- `sso` (Boolean) Require Pangolin SSO authentication. Defaults to `true`.
- `user_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the users granted access.
- `whitelist_emails` (Set of String) Emails allowed through the whitelist, in lowercase. `*@example.com` allows a whole domain. Requires `email_whitelist_enabled = true`: the server drops the list while the whitelist is disabled.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The numeric resource policy ID.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) The rule action: `ACCEPT`, `DROP`, or `PASS`.
- `match` (String) The match type: `CIDR`, `IP`, `PATH`, `COUNTRY`, `COUNTRY_IS_NOT`, `ASN`, `REGION`, or `METHOD`.
- `priority` (Number) The rule priority (lower number = higher priority).
- `value` (String) The value to match against (CIDR range, IP address, path, country or region code, ASN, HTTP method).

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enabled. Defaults to `true`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import pangolin_resource_policy.example <resource_policy_id>
```
